problem: Web agents and embodied agents are studied in isolation: web agents are confined to screens and embodied agents have no web access. No platform or benchmark tests tasks that need both, e.g. cooking from an online recipe or navigating with online map directions.
motivation: Humans fluidly switch between physical action and online information, and many real tasks need both (cooking from recipes, shopping and pickup, tourism, geolocation). Such tasks raise two challenges: grounding digital instructions in physical perception, and cross-domain planning about when to switch between realms.
key_idea: Introduce Embodied Web Agents, a unified simulation platform (AI2-THOR indoor, Google Street View outdoor, and five functional websites) together with a ~1.5k-task benchmark that requires coordinated web and embodied reasoning.
insight: The failure analysis for GPT-4o on cooking shows cross-domain errors are 66.6% of failures, versus 14.6% embodied and 8.0% web. The main failure modes are getting stuck in one domain and misaligning web instructions with embodied actions. Web-only accuracy consistently exceeds embodied-only accuracy, and completion rate is moderate while overall accuracy is very low, so models handle sub-parts but not integration. In geolocation, adding exploration plus Wikipedia querying improves every model over the static-image baseline.
method: Unified environment formalism: E=<S,A,O,T> with combined physical-digital state, an action space spanning both domains including switch_environment, and observations made of embodied input plus web perception.

Outdoor environment: a Google Street View navigation graph over New York, Boston, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh; nodes are GPS points with four directional images (N/E/S/W), and edges carry heading and distance. The agent picks a neighbor at each step.
Indoor environment: AI2-THOR kitchen scenes with tracked object states (isSliced, isCooked, parentReceptacles) and a state evaluator that compares the current state to target states.

Web environment: five functional websites. Recipe, shopping and homepage sites are custom-built (React frontend, FastAPI backend); OpenStreetMap and Wikipedia are adapted from WebArena. Observations are SoM screenshots or accessibility trees.

Benchmark construction: 144 navigation, 216 shopping, 110 traveling, 911 cooking and 142 geolocation tasks. Tasks are generated with GPT-4o-mini or Claude prompts, refined from online recipes, with confounder recipes, and human-verified. Navigation ground truth is the Dijkstra shortest path.
Evaluation metrics: Overall Accuracy (web and embodied both succeed), Web-only Accuracy, Embodied-only Accuracy and Overall Completion Rate.

Geolocation pipeline: the agent generates Wikipedia-style queries, runs them in VisualWebArena, and estimates its confidence. It moves to adjacent viewpoints until confident, then outputs a prediction. This is compared with the FairLocator single-image baseline.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Qwen-VL-Plus, InternVL2.5-latest (all frozen, prompted; Qwen-PLUS and InternLM for text-only cooking)
setting.training_data: none (training-free, prompted baselines on a benchmark)
setting.observation: Outdoor: four-direction street-view RGB images plus neighbor headings and distances and web screenshots. Indoor: first-person RGB or AI2-THOR scene graph, plus web screenshots (SoM) or accessibility trees.
setting.action_space: Outdoor: choose a neighbor node (Forward/Left/Right). Indoor: MoveAhead/Back/Left/Right, Teleport, PickupObject, PutObject, Open/Close, Slice, Cook. Web: click/type/scroll/hover/tab/goto, plus switch_environment.
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR + Google Street View/Earth + self-hosted websites (WebArena/VisualWebArena)

numbers_note: The benchmark is new and has no canonical name. Its splits are not specified, so 'test' is used for the whole benchmark. Table 1 labels the model 'GPT', but the text says GPT-4o-mini for outdoor tasks. Cooking tables are labelled GPT-4o. Qwen, Intern and Gemini rows are omitted from the numbers apart from the geolocation Gemini row.
results: Best agents (GPT/Gemini) reach only 34.72% (navigation), 25.46% (shopping), 30.91% (traveling) and 6.4% (cooking) overall accuracy, versus human 77-93%. In geolocation, embodied exploration with web access improves over the FairLocator static baseline for all models (e.g. GPT-4o-mini city-level 73.24 to 85.21).
limitations: Simulation only; no real robots, so real physical-digital unpredictability is not captured.
Only frozen prompted LLM baselines are evaluated; no dedicated method or training is proposed.
Geolocation street-level accuracy is very low (~4%), and the outdoor and indoor tasks use simplified discrete action spaces and self-hosted websites.
